– the failing test (signature + snippet),

– likely-relevant recent bug reports,

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testOptionGroupLong()` is failing because selecting an option with only a long option name (and no short name) in an OptionGroup does not work as expected. The test creates an OptionGroup and adds options with long options "foo" and "bar" using OptionBuilder, then parses the command line with "--bar" and asserts that "bar" is selected.

The current bug report says that OptionGroup doesn't handle options with only a long name well; `group.setSelected(option)` has no effect if the selected option lacks a short name.

Looking at the `OptionGroup.setSelected(Option option)` method:
- It checks `selected == null || selected.equals(option.getOpt())` before setting `selected = option.getOpt()`.
- The `selected` field stores the option's short name (`option.getOpt()`) as a string.

The `Option.getOpt()` method returns the short name of the option, which is `null` if the option only has a long option name.

In `OptionGroup.addOption(Option option)`, the option is stored in the map keyed by `option.getKey()`, which returns `opt` if non-null, otherwise `longOpt`.

The problem manifests because `OptionGroup.setSelected()` uses `option.getOpt()` to set the selected option, but for purely long options, `getOpt()` returns null. This means `selected` is set to null or not correctly set, so `getSelected()` returns null, failing the test.

In summary:
- Options with only long names have `opt` (short name) null.
- `setSelected()` incorrectly uses `option.getOpt()` to store selected option identifier instead of using `option.getKey()` which works for both short and long options.
- This causes selection of long-only options to fail.

Therefore, the root cause is that `OptionGroup.setSelected()` uses `option.getOpt()` (short name) instead of `option.getKey()` (which covers both short and long options) when setting the selected option.

This matches the symptom described in the bug report that "If the selected option hasn't a short name, group.setSelected(option) has no effect."

No other recent bugs are relevant to this issue.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure in the test `testOptionGroupLong()` occurs because the `OptionGroup` class does not properly handle options that have only a long name (no short name). The `setSelected` method of `OptionGroup` sets the selected option using `option.getOpt()`, which returns the short name of the option, and returns `null` for options with no short name. This causes the `selected` field to be set to `null` or incorrectly, and thus `getSelected()` returns `null` instead of the correct long option name. Meanwhile, options are stored internally in the group keyed by `option.getKey()`, which uses the long name if the short name is null. Thus, the root cause is that `OptionGroup.setSelected()` should be using `option.getKey()` rather than `option.getOpt()` to handle both short and long option names correctly. This mismatch leads to the failure of selecting pure long options within a group, matching the problem described in the bug report.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
